tasks.topic: A drawdown diagnostic passes through early overlapping pressure and derivative, then a flat derivative, and much later a rising unit-slope derivative.
tasks.goal: Identify the three time regimes without assigning the same physical cause to both unit-slope intervals, and explain what can be inferred from each.

success_criteria.description: Attribute early overlap and unit slope to wellbore storage, not radial flow.
Attribute the middle horizontal derivative to infinite-acting radial flow.
Treat the late unit slope as potentially bounded/semi-steady depletion, conditional on context, and cite at least two source pages.

claims.claim: Early pressure and logarithmic derivative overlap on a unit-slope line under wellbore storage.
The middle radial-flow derivative is constant or horizontal.
A later unit-slope response can signal bounded semi-steady-state depletion, not the early storage regime.

tasks.topic: A completion is open only across part of a thick producing interval.
tasks.goal: Explain how near-well flow geometry and anisotropy alter interpretation, and how the completion contribution enters an apparent skin estimate.

success_criteria.description: Distinguish local convergent/spherical flow from later radial flow.
Explain why vertical as well as radial permeability matters.
Identify a partial-penetration pseudo-skin and its geometrical dependence with sources.

claims.claim: Flow near a partly open well can be spherical/convergent and sensitive to vertical permeability; away from the well radial flow can develop.
Partial completion introduces pseudo-skin dependent on penetration ratio and geometry such as hs/rw.

tasks.topic: The same heterogeneous beds can be connected side by side or end to end relative to flow.
tasks.goal: State the physical boundary conditions, correct effective-permeability operators, and the engineering consequence of a low-permeability bed in each arrangement.

success_criteria.description: For parallel beds, state common pressure drop and thickness/area-weighted arithmetic permeability.
For series beds, state common rate and length-weighted harmonic permeability.
Explain why a low-k layer bottlenecks series flow more strongly than parallel flow, with both formula sources.

claims.claim: Parallel layers share pressure drop and their effective permeability is weighted arithmetic mean by thickness or area.
Series layers share flow rate, add pressure losses, and have length-weighted harmonic effective permeability; low k dominates resistance.

tasks.topic: Two wireline formation-pressure surveys have similar vertical coverage: one is virgin, the other follows substantial field production.
tasks.goal: Compare how to interpret pressure-depth trends, and explain why selected outliers or nonhydrostatic gradients cannot be handled by one universal rule.

success_criteria.description: Distinguish virgin hydrostatic/capillary interpretation from a produced dynamic pressure field.
Describe depletion/flow effects and possible compartment interpretation without asserting it from a single cloud.
Discuss supercharged points as a possible artifact requiring investigation rather than deleting all deviating points, with multi-page evidence.

claims.claim: Virgin pressure-depth profiles primarily reflect fluid gradients and capillarity, whereas produced-reservoir profiles are dynamic and can reflect pressure depletion and barriers.
Supercharging can affect WFT/RFT points, and screening requires supporting geological/permeability context; a produced profile need not be hydrostatic.

tasks.topic: A type-curve match is attempted on a pressure transient that displays an early unit-slope stem but no convincing middle-time derivative plateau.
tasks.goal: Separate what early data establish from what is still needed for an identifiable permeability interpretation; do not infer a boundary solely from the ideal type curve.

success_criteria.description: Interpret early unit slope as storage-dominated with little reservoir-property information.
Explain that missing radial plateau/pressure match weakens or blocks permeability identification.
Recognize that the cited infinite-acting storage+skin model has no late boundary region; separate model assumption from field proof.

claims.claim: Early unit slope reflects storage-dominated pD=tD/CD and provides little formation-property information.
Permeability needs pressure or derivative-plateau match; without a middle-time region the match is poorly constrained.
The infinite-acting storage+skin type curve lacks a late-time boundary regime by assumption, not proof that a real reservoir has no boundary.

tasks.topic: Three parallel producing layers have (h ft, k mD) = (10,80), (20,200), (5,500).
tasks.goal: Compute total thickness, effective flow-parallel permeability, and the high-k thin bed's fraction of total kh; explain the weighting.

success_criteria.description: Use the parallel thickness-weighted arithmetic formula from the KB.
Report 35 ft and k_eff near 208.57 mD.
Report the 5-ft 500-mD bed's kh share near 34.25% and interpret it.

claims.claim: For parallel beds, k_eff=sum(k_i h_i)/sum(h_i).

tasks.topic: Flow crosses three end-to-end beds of equal area: (length ft, permeability mD) = (10,40), (25,100), (15,250).
tasks.goal: Calculate the series effective permeability and the arithmetic length-weighted value that would be wrong for this geometry; quantify the overstatement percentage.

success_criteria.description: Use series length-weighted harmonic mean rather than parallel arithmetic mean.
Report series k_eff near 89.29 mD and arithmetic comparison 133 mD.
Quantify arithmetic overstatement near 48.96% relative to correct series value.

claims.claim: End-to-end beds have equal rate and additive pressure drop, so k_eff=sum(L_i)/sum(L_i/k_i).
Arithmetic weighting applies to parallel, not this series geometry.

tasks.topic: At comparable stabilized conditions, wells A/B/C have (oil rate STB/day, average reservoir pressure psia, flowing pressure psia): A=(450,3100,3000), B=(600,3100,2950), C=(550,3100,2990).
tasks.goal: Compute productivity index for each well in STB/day/psi, rank the wells by index rather than raw rate, and explain the change in ranking.

success_criteria.description: Use J=Q_o/(p_e-p_w) with consistent pressure units.
Report J_A=4.5, J_B=4.0 and J_C=5.0 STB/day/psi.
Rank C>A>B by index and distinguish from raw-rate ranking B>C>A.

claims.claim: The oil productivity index is oil rate divided by reservoir-to-flowing pressure drawdown.
Comparing normalized indices can reverse the ranking obtained from raw rates.

tasks.topic: A reservoir has area 2.0 million m^2, net thickness 12 m, porosity 0.18, initial water saturation 0.25, oil FVF Bo=1.20 reservoir m^3/stock-tank m^3, and assumed recovery factor 0.35.
tasks.goal: Estimate stock-tank oil initially in place and recoverable volume; recalculate OOIP if Sw rises to 0.30 with all else fixed, and report percentage change.

success_criteria.description: Apply A*h*phi*(1-Sw)/Bo with coherent cubic-metre units.
Report 2.70 million stock-tank m^3 OOIP and 0.945 million stock-tank m^3 recoverable at RF=0.35.
Report 2.52 million stock-tank m^3 at Sw=0.30 and a 6.67% reduction.

claims.claim: Stock-tank OOIP equals A*h*phi*(1-Sw)/Bo; recoverable volume additionally requires a recovery factor.

tasks.topic: Use the appraisal-well RFT depth/pressure table on Well Test Analysis page 81. Fit separate ordinary-least-squares pressure-on-depth lines to the first three rows (15200,6904), (15261,6906), (15305,6907) and to the seven rows from 15402 through 15628 ft: (15402,6936), (15415,6948), (15488,6972), (15505,6981), (15525,6991), (15556,7008), (15628,7044), with depth in ft and pressure in psia.
tasks.goal: Report both fitted gradients in psi/ft, compare their ratio, and avoid claiming a unique fluid contact from these two fitted subsets alone.

success_criteria.description: Use the KB RFT table and clearly state the two row subsets and OLS method.
Report shallow slope about 0.02883 and deeper slope about 0.46139 psi/ft.
Report deeper/shallow slope ratio about 16.00 and avoid unsupported exact contact inference.

claims.claim: The specified RFT depth/pressure pairs are present in the appraisal-well exercise table.
Two subset slopes alone do not uniquely locate a contact or prove its mechanism; geological and measurement context is needed.

numeric_targets.formula: OLS slope covariance(depth,pressure)/variance(depth) on first 3 specified rows
OLS slope on seven specified deeper rows

tasks.topic: A colleague labels the mid-time flat derivative on a log-log drawdown plot 'the unit-slope radial overlap'.
tasks.goal: Audit that label, correct the flow-regime attribution, and distinguish any legitimate later unit-slope interpretation.
tasks.expected_result: Radial flow has pressure and derivative overlapping at unit slope.

success_criteria.description: Explicitly reject radial unit-slope overlap as a false premise.
Assign early unit-slope overlap to storage and radial plateau to mid-time.
Mention late bounded/recharge unit slope only conditionally and cite sources.

claims.claim: Radial flow has a horizontal derivative; early unit-slope pressure-derivative overlap belongs to wellbore storage.
A later unit slope can arise from boundary/depletion or recharge depending on setting and is not the radial plateau.

tasks.topic: The same three beds have permeability 40, 100 and 250 mD, and lengths 10, 25 and 15 ft across the flow path.
tasks.goal: Test the proposed target that series effective permeability must be higher than the arithmetic length-weighted value because adding beds creates more flow channels.

success_criteria.description: Reject the more-channels premise for end-to-end beds.
Identify the series harmonic formula and note its bottleneck behavior.
Report series effective permeability about 89.29 mD, below 133 mD arithmetic comparison, with citations.

claims.claim: End-to-end series beds carry one common flow and their resistances add; parallel arithmetic weighting is inapplicable.
The required series permeability is below the arithmetic comparison, contradicting the proposed target.

tasks.topic: An RFT survey in a substantially produced reservoir shows a diffuse pressure-depth cloud and a few anomalous high-pressure points.
tasks.goal: Assess the instruction to force one virgin hydrostatic line through every point and declare all deviations measurement errors.
tasks.expected_result: A produced reservoir must remain hydrostatic, so all deviations are errors.

success_criteria.description: Reject mandatory virgin hydrostatic behavior after production.
Identify depletion, compartmentalization and supercharging as distinct possible explanations.
Avoid claiming any particular point is invalid without supporting context.

claims.claim: After production, WFT/RFT profiles can reflect dynamic depletion and need not follow a single hydrostatic gradient.
Supercharged points and compartment effects are interpretations requiring context; indiscriminate deletion of all deviations is not supported.

tasks.topic: Only the conceptual type-curve pages on wellbore storage and pressure matching are supplied; there is no field pressure/time curve, matched pressure ordinate, flow rate, viscosity, or pay thickness for a particular new well.
tasks.goal: Give that new well's exact permeability in mD and defend its uniqueness using only the KB.

success_criteria.description: State that exact well-specific permeability cannot be calculated from generic method pages alone.
Identify missing field match and flow/fluid/thickness inputs.
Give the applicable pressure-match method without fabricating a mD value.

claims.claim: Type-curve permeability depends on a measured pressure match and physical flow/fluid/thickness inputs unavailable for this well.
Early storage-dominated response alone is not sufficient formation-property evidence.

tasks.topic: A mapped reservoir has area 1.5 million m^2, net thickness 10 m, porosity 0.20, water saturation 0.25 and Bo 1.25, but no recovery factor, production history, drive-mechanism characterization or reserves estimate.
tasks.goal: Report a unique recoverable stock-tank oil volume, while distinguishing it from calculable initial oil in place.

success_criteria.description: Compute initial stock-tank oil in place as 1.8 million m^3.
State that recoverable reserves cannot be uniquely inferred without recovery factor.
Do not substitute OOIP for reserves or invent an RF; cite both source pages.

claims.claim: Stock-tank oil in place follows A*h*phi*(1-Sw)/Bo.
Recoverable reserves need an RF and cannot be uniquely inferred from volumetric input alone.

tasks.topic: A produced-field RFT pressure-depth scatter is supplied, but there are no pressure-transient tests, cross-well interference tests, production allocation data, or verified lithology for the new interval.
tasks.goal: Name the exact fault transmissibility in mD-ft, specify precisely which two wells communicate, and give a unique compartment boundary depth.

success_criteria.description: Mark the requested transmissibility/communication/depth values undetermined by the supplied scatter alone.
Explain plausible dynamic and supercharging confounders.
List the specific additional tests/data needed rather than fabricating a unique interpretation.

claims.claim: Produced RFT pressure-depth scatter can reflect dynamic depletion, barriers and supercharging; it does not uniquely determine fault transmissibility or cross-well connectivity.
Further time-dependent or cross-well pressure evidence and geological context are needed for a unique quantitative fault interpretation.

tasks.topic: Inspect the appraisal-well RFT survey labelled Figure 2 in Well Test Analysis, PDF page 440, together with the adjacent explanatory text.
tasks.goal: Identify the plotted pressure-depth variables and oil-gradient interpretation, and explain why anomalous points should not redefine the main line without corroboration.

success_criteria.description: Identify Figure 2 and the correct page/image, not Figure 1 or Figure 3.
State pressure versus TVD and the approximately 0.34 psi/ft oil gradient from adjacent text.
Discuss supercharged anomalous points and distinguish them from the main trend.

claims.claim: The appraisal-well Figure 2 shows pressure against TVD and the adjacent text interprets an oil gradient near 0.34 psi/ft.
A few supercharged RFT points can deviate from the dominant oil-gradient trend.

tasks.topic: Compare the raw and interpreted Venezuela RFT surveys labelled Figures 4 and 5 on Well Test Analysis PDF page 441, using the explanatory text on the previous page.
tasks.goal: Explain what interpretation changed between the two plots and which conclusions remain conditional rather than directly measured.

success_criteria.description: Map raw Figure 4 and interpreted Figure 5 to the two correct images on page 441.
Explain screening of supercharged points with shale/permeability context and grouping into pressure zones.
Avoid claiming the raw cloud alone proves a single hydrostatic gradient or exact communication mechanism.

claims.claim: Figure 4 is raw Venezuela RFT scatter and Figure 5 is its interpretation.

Interpretation screens supercharged readings using shale/permeability context and separates pressure zones; raw produced-field data need not be hydrostatic and do not alone prove a unique communication mechanism.
